correctness.rationale: Reflecting the mandatory base across arbitrary center (u,t) forces two translated base sections, hence a slab of sectional volume at least A at every intermediate height; the reflected apex pair forces disjoint outside caps of minimal volume Aq/d each. Integrating gives three sharp lower branches. Choosing horizontal center u=0 and convex hull of T and reflected T realizes each with no horizontal enlargement because a and -a belong to B. For d>=3 the height profile uniquely minimizes at t=0; nonzero u strictly increases B+[0,2u] and its cap volumes; equality forces unique center and hull. For d=2 the middle slope vanishes. Independent SciPy ConvexHull calculations for 5 heights and an off-axis square-pyramid model reproduced predicted volumes, but analytic cap argument is the all-dimensional proof.
